Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21625 of 2023

Applicant :- Sanjay Kumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Prashant Kumar,Devendra Kumar Yadav

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Devendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha,
learned brief holder for the State.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
04 of 2023, under Sections 389, 419, 420, 170, 171 IPC and Section 3/25 Arms Act, Police Station Dulhapur, District Ghazipur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged by informant who is the police person and according to the informant applicantpersonatinghimself as police Sub Inspector and demanded Rs. 10,000/- as illegal gratification by stating that a girl has made a complaint of rape against him but when informant made search of applicant, then he found that applicant in fact, not a police personnel.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant did not personate himself to be a Sub Inspector and he has been falsely implicated by the informant who himself is a police personnel.

He further submitted that actually applicant was having previous criminal history of similar nature and only due to this Sanjay Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27278621/
1 reason applicant has been implicated in the present matter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. He further submitted that it is hard to believe that by personating himself to be a police officer applicant demanded illegal gratification from another police personnel and this fact itself shows that FIR is based on false and frivolous allegation.

He next submits that actually informant knew the applicant quite well as applicant has given Rs. 1,00,000/- Lac to him as loan but when applicant demanded back his money then instead of returning his money, informant implicated him in the present matter.
He further submitted that criminal history of the applicant has been explained in Paragraph No. 15 and 16 of the affidavit and applicant is in jail since 07.01.2023.

6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant used to commit such type of offences and earlier also he was apprehended while he was personating himself to be a police officer and this time again he personated himself to be a police Sub Inspector.

Therefore,
considering the background of the applicant he should not be released on bail but could not dispute the fact that informant of the case himself a police personnel and as per allegation, applicant tried to dupe the police personnel by personating himself to be a police officer.
7.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
8. Although, as per allegation application personating himself to be a police Sub Inspector and demanded illegal gratification of Rs. 10,000/- from the informant
and he is also having criminal history of three cases and out three cases two cases were of Section 170 IPC and personated himself to be a police officer

but from the record it reflects that informant is himself a police personnel and,
therefore, argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that it is hard to believe that applicant by personating himself to be a police officer tried to dupe a police personnel cannot be brushed aside at this stage.
9. Therefore, from the discussion made above, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10.

Let the applicant-Sanjay Kumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
